sources.title: GLM-5.3-Flash: How to Run Locally - unsloth.ai
sources.snippet: GLM-5.3-Flash can now run locally in Unsloth Desktop! GLM-5.3-Flash was trained on 30T tokens and is built on a newly trained base model redesigned. Its hybrid sparse and linear attention architecture lowers long-context serving costs without sacrificing accuracy, while Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections improve scaling.

sources.title: GLM-5.3-Flash - lmstudio.ai
sources.snippet: GLM-5.3-Flash is Z.ai's first natively multimodal model in the GLM-5 series. It is a 320B Mixture-of-Experts model with 18B active parameters, built for coding, agentic work, and visual tasks, and released under the MIT License.

sources.title: GitHub - 0xSero/glm-5.3-flash-sglang-sm120: Exact SGLang runtime for ...
sources.snippet: Locked, independently buildable representation of the live Pop!_OS deployment (glm-5.3-flash-sglang-sm120). Uses the exact lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash image digest and preserves the effective server arguments and environment from the validated running container. The 182 GiB checkpoint is intentionally not copied into the image.

sources.title: GLM-5.3: Frontier Coding with Emergent Cyber Capabilities - z.ai
sources.snippet: Today we are releasing GLM-5.3. It uses the same base model as GLM-5.2 — every gain comes from post-training. Compared with GLM-5.2, it is much better at complex coding and long-horizon tasks: Stronger Coding: GLM-5.3 is the most capable open-weights model for coding, with a 50% improvement over GLM-5.2 on our in-house Z.ai Code Bench.
